text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Interest payments on the public debt in October increased the budget deficit to 54.18 percent.
-Police seized 25 tonnes of putrid meat in Beirut port on a cargo ship coming from India.
-The constitutional council set up four committies among its 10 members to begin studying 19 appeals from defeated candidates against the results of recent parliamentary elections.
-A Lebanese surgeon in Beirut made the first open-heart operation in the Middle East via satellite in coordination with a surgeon in France.
-Prime minister Hariri denied that he intends to privatise the telephone service in Lebanon.
-Lebanon's school teachers stage one-day strike today for pay scale demands.
-One pro-Israeli militiaman was killed and another one was wounded after Hizbollah guerrillas attacked their post in south Lebanon.
-Israeli forces kidnapped three citizens in south Lebanon.
-A meeting at the house of former prime minister Salim el-Hoss prepares for opposition parliamentary gathering.
-Solidere shares fell on the Beirut Stock Exchange on oversupply of its shares.
-Environmental watchdog group Greenpeace condemns what it calls Germany's procrastination in taking back toxic waste shipped to Lebanon.
